_note: What each town sells, for ever. A shelf is content: it does not roll, it does not reroll, and a save records only which entries have been bought. Order is part of the contract — a purchase is stored as a town and an index — so append to a list, never insert into the middle of one.
_shape: Each town is a place rather than a slot machine in a costume. The End of All Gears has the cheap basics and nothing else; Kettleworks is metalwork, and is where a real helmet and a second blade come from; High Wick is the arcane shelf and the only place a book, an ink and a spell can be bought together.

towns._note: The pit's own town, and everything on it is under six Fnorp. A starting character has twenty-eight and owns a handle and a blade, so this shelf is one finished helmet and one pair of gloves, or most of both.
Metalwork. Plate, gauntlets and edges — the things the slag flats are made of.
The arcane shelf, and the only one that sells a book, an ink and a spell in the same room — which is the whole of what makes a caster weapon buildable at all.
